title: APM/PM Core 6 Analytics Stack
description: The 6 essential analytics concepts for APM/PM interviews (0-2 years experience), covering ~85% of what interviews actually test
target_companies: All — FAANG, startup, SaaS, growth stage

core_6.why_essential: The single most common APM question: 'something is dropping off, walk me through how you'd investigate.' You need a structured answer every time — not just knowing what a funnel is.
answer_structure: Quantify the drop at each step as a percentage
Identify the single biggest drop by volume × value
Segment that step by platform, device, acquisition channel, user tenure
Propose validation method (session replay, survey, A/B test)
core_6.example_answer: Funnel: Homepage (100%) → Signup (42%) → Step 1 (38%) → Step 2 (21%) → Activation (14%). Biggest drop is Step 1→2 at 45%. I'd segment by platform — if iOS drops harder, it's likely a UI bug. Run session replays on step 2. Fix the top friction point and A/B test.
core_6.common_mistake: Naming the funnel steps without prioritizing which drop to fix first, or not segmenting the biggest drop

core_6.why_essential: 'Retention dropped' is asked in every PM loop. You need to know what a retention curve shape means, what cohort comparison reveals, and how to separate signal from mix shift. D1/D7/D30 benchmarks must be instant recall.

benchmarks.pmf_signal: Retention curve flattens = product-market fit achieved

answer_structure: State current D1/D7/D30 numbers and benchmark against industry
Pull cohort chart — compare recent cohorts vs older ones
If newer cohorts worse: either product regressed or acquisition channel changed
Segment by acquisition source to disentangle product quality vs user intent
Identify the D7→D30 drop — that is the habit-formation gap to fix
Recommend intervention: onboarding improvement, re-engagement trigger, feature fix
core_6.example_answer: D30 retention dropped from 28% to 18%. Cohort chart shows Jan cohort at 28%, March at 18% — the drop coincides with our pricing change in Feb. New users are lower-intent. Segment by acquisition channel: paid users churn 2x faster than organic. Fix: improve activation for paid users or adjust targeting.
core_6.common_mistake: Looking at aggregate retention without cohort breakdown — misses whether it's a product regression or a mix-shift problem

core_6.why_essential: Every company that ships features tests them. You must state the full framework: hypothesis → primary metric + guardrail → sample size logic → runtime → ship decision. Saying 'run an A/B test' without the rest fails this question.

full_framework.step_1_hypothesis: If we [change X], then [metric Y] will improve by [Z%] because [reason]
full_framework.step_2_metrics: Primary metric (what you're optimizing) + 2 guardrail metrics (what you won't sacrifice)
full_framework.step_3_sample_size: Use baseline rate, MDE, α=0.05, power=80% to calculate minimum n per arm
full_framework.step_4_runtime: Min 2 weeks to cover weekly seasonality. Don't peek before reaching sample size.
full_framework.step_5_ship_decision: Ship if p<0.05 AND confidence interval fully above zero AND guardrails not broken

core_6.example_answer: Hypothesis: simplifying checkout step 2 will lift conversion by 3%. Primary metric: checkout completion rate. Guardrails: D7 retention, average order value. Sample size: baseline 5% CVR, 1pp MDE, need ~3,800 users/arm. With 500/day per arm = 8 days. Run 2 weeks. Ship if CI is [+1%, +5%] — fully positive.
core_6.common_mistake: Saying 'run an A/B test' without specifying guardrail metrics, sample size rationale, or ship decision criteria

core_6.why_essential: 'DAU dropped 15% overnight — what do you do?' is one of the most common APM questions. You need a repeatable investigation structure. Speed and structure win here.
investigation_structure: Step 1 — Rule out data issues: check pipeline, logging, instrumentation. Is the drop real?
Step 2 — Check magnitude: how many SDs from mean? 2σ = investigate, 3σ = almost certainly real
Step 3 — Segment to isolate: platform, geography, user segment, feature area
Step 4 — Correlate with events: deployments, outages, competitor launches, external news
Step 5 — Hypothesize causes ranked by probability
Step 6 — Validate fastest hypothesis first, then act
core_6.example_answer: DAU dropped 12% Thursday. Step 1: check data pipeline — no issues. Step 2: 3.6 SDs below mean — real signal. Step 3: segment by platform — iOS down 25%, Android flat. Step 4: iOS build deployed Wednesday. Conclusion: iOS bug. Hot-fix immediately, then do post-mortem.
core_6.common_mistake: Jumping to product hypotheses without first ruling out data pipeline issues and segmenting to isolate the variable

core_6.why_essential: Every 'how would you measure success of X?' question requires this. Pick one north star that captures core value delivery, define 2 guardrails. Without guardrails you sound junior.

north_star_examples.north_star: DAU or time spent per DAU
Weekly active teams or seats used

answer_structure: Identify what core value the product delivers to users
Define north star as the metric that best captures that value delivery at scale
Define 2 guardrails — one for user experience, one for business health
Explain why the north star is leading (predicts future health) not lagging
core_6.example_answer: For a food delivery app, north star = successful orders completed per week. This captures value for both user (food delivered) and business (revenue). Guardrails: delivery time (user experience) and restaurant partner retention (supply health). I'd avoid GMV as north star — it's lagging and inflatable via discounts.
core_6.common_mistake: Picking a vanity metric (signups, downloads, page views) as north star, or defining no guardrails

core_6.why_essential: Not a standalone tool — a habit applied to every answer. Interviewers explicitly look for this. Candidates who give aggregate answers without segmenting read as analytically shallow.
default_segmentation_dimensions: User tenure (new <7 days, growing 7-30 days, retained 30+ days)
User type (free vs paid, casual vs power user)
Device type (mobile vs desktop, screen size)
core_6.how_to_apply: In every metric answer, after stating the aggregate number, immediately say: 'I'd break this down by platform, user tenure, and acquisition channel to see if the trend is uniform or isolated to a segment.'
core_6.example_answer: Overall DAU is flat — but I'd never stop there. Breaking by platform: web DAU down 20%, mobile DAU up 35%. The product is shifting mobile-first and we've been optimizing the wrong surface. Breaking by tenure: new users down 40%, retained users flat — it's an acquisition or onboarding problem, not a retention problem.
core_6.common_mistake: Giving aggregate metric answers without segmentation — the #1 signal that a candidate thinks at surface level

metric_deep_dive.description: Something dropped — walk me through how you'd investigate
metric_deep_dive.answer_flow: Segment first → isolate the drop → funnel to find the step → RCA to find the cause → recommend fix

experiment_design.description: How would you test / validate this feature?
experiment_design.answer_flow: Hypothesis → metrics + guardrails → sample size → runtime → ship decision → segment results

product_health_diagnosis.description: How would you assess if this product is healthy?
product_health_diagnosis.answer_flow: State north star → check retention curve shape → cohort breakdown → segment by user type → diagnosis

estimation_sizing.description: Estimate X, size market Y, how many users do Z?
estimation_sizing.answer_flow: Anchor on north star metric → segment population into buckets → estimate each bucket → sanity check total
estimation_sizing.note: Estimation is structured thinking with segmentation, not arithmetic. The north star anchors what you're estimating.

what_to_deprioritize_at_apm_level.note: These are real concepts but secondary for 0-2 year PM interviews. Learn them as depth when interviewers push back — not as primary answers.

deprioritized.why: More relevant for growth PM or senior PM roles, not core APM analytics
Know that p<0.05 = significant and CI matters more — don't recite the formula
Know the concept (2σ = anomaly) but don't derive it in interviews
Useful but rarely the primary chart in an APM interview — mention as supporting detail
Know the concept (need enough traffic to detect MDE) — calculators handle the math

rapid_practice_triggers.question: DAU dropped 15% overnight. What do you do?
Our checkout conversion fell from 5% to 3%. Walk me through your analysis.
How would you measure success of a new notification feature?
We want to test a new onboarding flow. How would you design the experiment?
